title: Validity of the doubled-word run
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $w$ be a Boolean word whose last bit is true whenever $w$ is nonempty. Suppose the input is the pair encoding of the word of $n$ ones and $w$. Then the doubled-input machine has a run from its initial configuration, with input head at position $1$, empty output, and work-tape head at $0$, to a configuration with input head at position $1$, work-tape head at $0$, and state yes exactly when $w$ is the binary expansion of $2n$, and no otherwise. Throughout the run, at every time before its endpoint, the work-tape head position lies between $-1$ and the length of the binary expansion of $2n$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: The input $y$ equals the pair encoding of $n$ ones and $w$
